Native HDR uses the direct Android video surface. GPU filters and Vulkan output are paused for this video.
Process HDR on the GPU

Processes HDR10 through Vulkan (gpu-next) for HDR-safe shaders. A confirmed PQ/BT.2020 surface does not prove that the TV displays HDR. Dolby Vision, HLG and HDR10+ on HDR10+ displays stay direct. Failed surface negotiation or sustained dropped frames return playback to direct output.
Process HDR on the GPU: HDR10 output surface confirmed (PQ/BT.2020). Physical display HDR mode unknown.

Process HDR on the GPU: checking the HDR10 output surface (Vulkan). Physical display mode unknown.

HDR output through the GPU: sharpening, deband and the RAVU Lite / FSR upscalers apply. Film grain is off here; denoise, deblock, SSimSuperRes, picture adjustments and the other shaders need SDR.
Process HDR on the GPU: no HDR-safe shader or deband is selected, so HDR stays on the direct surface.
The default output “Direct” stays in place for SDR; HDR10 uses the GPU route as long as a shader or deband is selected. Choosing “Direct” in the player or a title profile keeps HDR direct.
HDR: only HDR-safe shaders (sharpening, RAVU Lite / FSR luma, deband) apply; chroma and SSim shaders are skipped.
